code: # the HGDP data (1043 individuals typed at about 650k loci) and the # population of each individual, as used in the benchmark of tidypopgen. # Each file is downloaded under a temporary name, so that an interrupted # download is not mistaken for a complete file when the script is run again zenodo_url <- "https://zenodo.org/records/15582364/files/" hgdp_files <- c(   "hgdp650.qc.hg19.bed", "hgdp650.qc.hg19.bim", "hgdp650.qc.hg19.fam",   "hgdp650_id_pop.txt" ) options(timeout = max(3600, getOption("timeout"))) for (file in hgdp_files) {   path <- file.path(hgdp_dir, file)   if (!file.exists(path)) {     download.file(paste0(zenodo_url, file), paste0(path, ".part"), mode = "wb")     file.rename(paste0(path, ".part"), path)   } } library(tidypopgen) hgdp <- gen_tibble(   file.path(hgdp_dir, "hgdp650.qc.hg19.bed"),   backingfile = file.path(gt_dir, "hgdp_raw"),   quiet = TRUE ) # loci with less than 5% of missing genotypes, as recommended in the manual # of ADMIXTURE, and polymorphic (fastmixture stops on monomorphic loci) hgdp <- hgdp |>   select_loci_if(loci_missingness(genotypes) < 0.05) |>   select_loci_if(loci_maf(genotypes) > 0) # LD clumping with the thresholds of the manual of ADMIXTURE (plink # --indep-pairwise 50 10 0.1). Clumping needs complete genotypes, so the # missing ones are imputed first (on a backing file with only the loci kept # above). loci_ld_clump() uses the imputed genotypes, but the gen_tibble # keeps using the raw ones, which are those written to the bed file below: # missing genotypes remain missing for all the tools hgdp <- gt_update_backingfile(   hgdp,   backingfile = file.path(gt_dir, "hgdp_filtered"),   quiet = TRUE ) set.seed(1) hgdp <- gt_impute_simple(hgdp, method = "random") hgdp <- hgdp |>   select_loci_if(     loci_ld_clump(genotypes, thr_r2 = 0.1, size = 50, use_positions = FALSE)   ) gt_as_plink(hgdp, file = file.path(hgdp_dir, "hgdp_bench.bed")) # a small subset to check the benchmark scripts (on which ADMIXTURE takes # about 30 s on one core): every 5th individual, and 25,000 of the loci that # are still polymorphic among them hgdp_quick <- hgdp[seq(1, nrow(hgdp), by = 5), ] |>   select_loci_if(loci_maf(genotypes) > 0) n_loci <- count_loci(hgdp_quick) set.seed(2) quick_loci <- seq_len(n_loci) %in% sample(n_loci, min(25000, n_loci)) hgdp_quick <- select_loci_if(hgdp_quick, quick_loci) gt_as_plink(hgdp_quick, file = file.path(hgdp_dir, "hgdp_bench_quick.bed"))

-s "$time_log" ]]; then     echo "NA"     return   fi   rss=$(awk '/Maximum resident set size \(kbytes\)/ { printf "%.1f", $NF / 1024; exit }' "$time_log")   if [[ -z "$rss" ]]; then     rss=$(awk '/maximum resident set size/ { printf "%.1f", $1 / 1048576; exit }' "$time_log")   fi   echo "${rss:-NA}" }  # the first match of a regular expression (with one group, which is # returned) at the start of a line of a log, or NA if there is none extract() {   local value   value=$(sed -n -E "s/$1/\1/p" "$2" | head -n 1)   echo "${value:-NA}" }  # Each program is run by a function run_<program> <cores> <cross-validation # (TRUE or FALSE)> <run directory> <seed> <start (random or svd)>.  # ADMIXTURE writes its output in the current directory, named after the bed # file (e.g. hgdp_bench.5.Q), so it is run from the directory of the run; # its log is what it prints. It starts from random values run_admixture() {   local n_cores=$1 crossval=$2 run_dir=$3 seed=$4   local bed_path=$PWD/$bed   local time_log=$PWD/$run_dir/time.log   local args=(-s "$seed" -j"$n_cores")   if [[ $crossval == TRUE ]]; then     args+=(--cv="$n_folds")   fi   (cd "$run_dir" && timed_exec "$time_log" admixture.log "$admixture" "${args[@]}" "$bed_path" "$k") }  # fastmixture writes its output (Q, P and a log with its settings and # results) with the prefix given by --out, and prints its progress. It # starts from an SVD of the genotypes, or from random values with # --random-init run_fastmixture() {   local n_cores=$1 crossval=$2 run_dir=$3 seed=$4 init=$5   local args=(     --bfile "${bed%.bed}" --K "$k" --threads "$n_cores" --seed "$seed"     --out "$run_dir/fastmixture"   )   if [[ $crossval == TRUE ]]; then     args+=(--cv "$n_folds")   fi   if [[ $init == random ]]; then     args+=(--random-init)   fi   timed_exec "$run_dir/time.log" "$run_dir/console.log" "$fastmixture" "${args[@]}" }  # ADAMIXTURE writes its output (Q, P and a plot) in --save_dir, named after # --name and K (e.g. adamixture.5.Q), and prints its progress. We pass # --chrom_mode all explicitly and set OMP_NUM_THREADS before starting it so # its OpenMP thread pool matches n_cores. In ADAMIXTURE >= 1.9, it starts # from an SVD of the genotypes followed by alternating least squares # (--init svd, its default), or from random values primed with EM steps # (--init random) run_adamixture() {   local n_cores=$1 crossval=$2 run_dir=$3 seed=$4 init=$5   local args=(     --data_path "$bed" --save_dir "$run_dir" --name adamixture -k "$k"     -t "$n_cores" -s "$seed" --chrom_mode all --device cpu --init "$init"   )   if [[ $crossval == TRUE ]]; then     args+=(--cv "$n_folds")   fi   timed_exec "$run_dir/time.log" "$run_dir/console.log" \     env OMP_NUM_THREADS="$n_cores" "$adamixture" "${args[@]}" }  # gt_radmix() is run by a new R process, which loads tidygenclust, reads the # bed file into a gen_tibble, runs gt_radmix() (from random values, its # default, or with init = "svd"), saves the results, and prints the # log-likelihood and cross-validation error run_radmix_cli() {   local n_cores=$1 crossval=$2 run_dir=$3 seed=$4 init=$5   timed_exec "$run_dir/time.log" "$run_dir/console.log" \     "$rscript" code/admixture_benchmark_radmix_cli.R "$bed" "$k" "$seed" \     "$n_cores" "$crossval" "$n_folds" "$run_dir" "$init" }  # julia, with the variables that activating its conda environment would # set, so that it finds the packages installed in it (without the time # taken by conda run) julia_run() {   env JULIA_DEPOT_PATH="$julia_prefix/share/julia:" \     JULIA_PROJECT="@$julia_env" JULIA_LOAD_PATH="@:@$julia_env:@stdlib" \     "$julia_prefix/bin/julia" "$@" }  # OpenADMIXTURE.jl is run by a new Julia process, which writes Q and P with # the prefix openadmixture, and prints its progress, the log-likelihood and # the time of the fit (Julia is started without an interactive thread, see # admixture_benchmark_openadmixture.jl); it starts from random values, and # has no cross-validation run_openadmixture_cli() {   local n_cores=$1 run_dir=$3 seed=$4   timed_exec "$run_dir/time.log" "$run_dir/console.log" \     env JULIA_DEPOT_PATH="$julia_prefix/share/julia:" \     JULIA_PROJECT="@$julia_env" JULIA_LOAD_PATH="@:@$julia_env:@stdlib" \     "$julia_prefix/bin/julia" --threads="$n_cores,0" \     code/admixture_benchmark_openadmixture.jl \     "$bed" "$k" "$seed" "$run_dir/openadmixture" }  # the same, after a warm-up on the small subset of the data, so that the # fit, timed in Julia, does not include compiling the code run_openadmixture() {   local n_cores=$1 run_dir=$3 seed=$4   timed_exec "$run_dir/time.log" "$run_dir/console.log" \     env JULIA_DEPOT_PATH="$julia_prefix/share/julia:" \     JULIA_PROJECT="@$julia_env" JULIA_LOAD_PATH="@:@$julia_env:@stdlib" \     "$julia_prefix/bin/julia" --threads="$n_cores,0" \     code/admixture_benchmark_openadmixture.jl \     "$bed" "$k" "$seed" "$run_dir/openadmixture" "$warmup_bed" } # each run is done in its own directory, and its time includes starting the # program, reading the data and saving the results. Its Q matrix and log are # then copied to the results, and its time, log-likelihood, cross-validation # error and number of iterations (extracted from its log) are added to a # table (csv file) run_and_record() {   local tool=$1 n_cores=$2 crossval=$3 seed=$4 init=$5 run=$6 table=$7   local run_dir=$runs_dir/$run start seconds q_file log_file loglik cv_error   local iterations iterations_pattern='^Converged in ([0-9]+) iterations.*'   rm -rf "$run_dir"   mkdir -p "$run_dir"   echo "Running $run"   start=$(now)   "run_$tool" "$n_cores" "$crossval" "$run_dir" "$seed" "$init"   seconds=$(awk -v start="$start" -v end="$(now)" \     'BEGIN { printf "%.3f", end - start }')   case $tool in     admixture)       q_file=$run_dir/$(basename "$bed" .bed).$k.Q       log_file=$run_dir/admixture.log       loglik=$(extract '^Loglikelihood: ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       cv_error=$(extract \         '^CV error \(K=[0-9]+\): ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       ;;     fastmixture)       q_file=$run_dir/fastmixture.K$k.s$seed.Q       log_file=$run_dir/fastmixture.K$k.s$seed.log       loglik=$(extract \         '^Final log-likelihood: ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       cv_error=$(extract \         '^Cross-validation error \(SD\): ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       ;;     adamixture)       q_file=$run_dir/adamixture.$k.Q       log_file=$run_dir/console.log       loglik=$(extract \         '^ *Final log-likelihood: ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       cv_error=$(extract \         '^ *K=[0-9]+: CV index = ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       # (the lines indented further are those of the initialisation)       iterations_pattern='^ {4}Converged at iteration ([0-9]+).*'       ;;     radmix_cli)       q_file=$run_dir/radmix.Q       log_file=$run_dir/radmix.log       loglik=$(extract '^Loglikelihood: ([^[:space:]]+).*' \         "$run_dir/console.log")       cv_error=$(extract '^CV error \(K=[0-9]+\): ([^[:space:]]+).*' \         "$run_dir/console.log")       ;;     openadmixture*)       q_file=$run_dir/openadmixture.Q       log_file=$run_dir/console.log       loglik=$(extract '^Loglikelihood: ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       cv_error=NA       iterations_pattern='^Main algorithm converged in ([0-9]+) iterations.*'       if [[ $tool == openadmixture ]]; then         # after the warm-up, the time of the fit alone         seconds=$(extract '^Fit time \(s\): ([^[:space:]]+).*' "$log_file")       fi       ;;   esac   iterations=$(extract "$iterations_pattern" "$log_file")   local peak_rss_mb   peak_rss_mb=$(extract_peak_rss_mb "$run_dir/time.log")   cp "$q_file" "$out_dir/Q/$run.Q"   cp "$log_file" "$out_dir/logs/$run.log"   echo "$tool,$init,$seed,$n_cores,$crossval,$seconds,$loglik,$cv_error,$iterations,$peak_rss_mb" \     >> "$table" } mkdir -p "$out_dir/Q" "$out_dir/logs" header=tool,init,seed,n_cores,crossval,seconds,loglik,cv_error,iterations,peak_rss_mb # all the programs from random starting values: each combination of # program, number of cores and cross-validation (or not) is run once (e.g. # admixture_t4_cv for ADMIXTURE on 4 cores with cross-validation). # OpenADMIXTURE.jl, which has no cross-validation, is run without it, both # from the command line (openadmixture_cli) and after a warm-up # (openadmixture, timed in Julia) timings=$out_dir/timings_cli.csv echo "$header" > "$timings" for tool in admixture fastmixture adamixture radmix_cli openadmixture_cli \   openadmixture; do   for n_cores in "${cores[@]}"; do     for crossval in FALSE TRUE; do       if [[ $crossval == TRUE && $tool == openadmixture* ]]; then         continue       fi       if [[ $crossval == TRUE ]]; then         run=${tool}_t${n_cores}_cv       else         run=${tool}_t${n_cores}_nocv       fi       run_and_record "$tool" "$n_cores" "$crossval" "$seed" random "$run" \         "$timings"     done   done done # the programs that can start from an SVD of the genotypes as well as from # random values, from each start with each seed, on the largest number of # cores, without cross-validation (e.g. fastmixture_svd_s2 for fastmixture # from an SVD with seed 2) starts=$out_dir/starts_cli.csv echo "$header" > "$starts" for tool in fastmixture adamixture radmix_cli; do   for init in random svd; do     for start_seed in "${start_seeds[@]}"; do       run_and_record "$tool" "${cores[-1]}" FALSE "$start_seed" "$init" \         "${tool}_${init}_s$start_seed" "$starts"     done   done done args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE) bed_file <- args[1] k <- as.integer(args[2]) seed <- as.integer(args[3]) n_cores <- as.integer(args[4]) crossval <- as.logical(args[5]) n_folds <- as.integer(args[6]) run_dir <- args[7] init <- args[8] library(tidygenclust) # BLAS is limited to the cores of the run: gt_radmix() can use it for the # PCA of init = "svd" (tidypopgen's gt_pca(), which handles missing # genotypes without imputation), and otherwise only for small k x k systems bigparallelr::set_blas_ncores(n_cores) hgdp <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(   bed_file,   backingfile = file.path(run_dir, "hgdp_bench"),   quiet = TRUE ) fit <- gt_radmix(   hgdp,   k = k,   seed = seed,   init = init,   crossval = crossval,   n_folds = n_folds,   n_cores = n_cores ) saveRDS(fit, file.path(run_dir, "radmix.rds")) # the Q matrix (one row per individual, with 6 decimals, as ADMIXTURE writes # it) and the log q <- fit$Q[[1]] write.table(   matrix(sprintf("%.6f", q), nrow = nrow(q)),   file.path(run_dir, "radmix.Q"),   quote = FALSE,   row.names = FALSE,   col.names = FALSE ) writeLines(fit$log[[1]], file.path(run_dir, "radmix.log")) cat(sprintf("Loglikelihood: %.6f\n", fit$loglik)) if (crossval) {   cat(sprintf("CV error (K=%d): %.6f\n", k, fit$cv)) } using OpenADMIXTURE, Printf, Random  bed, k, seed, prefix = ARGS[1], parse(Int, ARGS[2]), parse(Int, ARGS[3]), ARGS[4] warmup = length(ARGS) >= 5 ? ARGS[5] : nothing  # a matrix written with one row per line, as ADMIXTURE writes its Q and P # matrices (6 decimals) function write_matrix(file, m)     open(file, "w") do io         for i in axes(m, 1)             println(io, join([@sprintf("%.6f", x) for x in m[i, :]], " "))         end     end end  if warmup !== nothing     OpenADMIXTURE.run_admixture(warmup, k; rng=Xoshiro(seed), admix_n_iter=1,         progress_bar=false) end  seconds = @elapsed begin     # sparsity = nothing (the default): all the loci are used     d, _, _ = OpenADMIXTURE.run_admixture(bed, k; rng=Xoshiro(seed), progress_bar=false)     # d.q and d.p have one column per individual and per locus     write_matrix(prefix * ".Q", permutedims(d.q))     write_matrix(prefix * ".P", permutedims(d.p)) end println("Loglikelihood: ", @sprintf("%.6f", d.ll_new)) println("Fit time (s): ", @sprintf("%.3f", seconds))

code: library(tidygenclust) # gt_radmix() runs in parallel with OpenMP (with n_cores threads); from a # random start it only uses BLAS for small (k x k) systems. BLAS is limited # to the cores of each run (below), so that a multithreaded BLAS does not # use more cores than requested # the same settings as in admixture_benchmark_cli.sh k <- 5 seed <- 1 n_folds <- 5 cores <- c(1, 2, 4, 8) # the Q matrices are written as ADMIXTURE and fastmixture write theirs (one # row per individual, with 6 decimals) write_q <- function(q, file) {   q_text <- matrix(sprintf("%.6f", q), nrow = nrow(q))   write.table(q_text, file, quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE) } # each combination of number of cores and cross-validation (or not) is run # once, in its own directory. As ADMIXTURE and fastmixture read the bed file # and write their estimates, the time of each run includes reading the bed # file into a gen_tibble (with its backing file in the directory of the # run), and saving the gt_admix object (with Q and P) to an RDS file. Its Q # matrix and log are then saved with the results, and its log-likelihood, # cross-validation error and number of iterations are recorded timings <- list() for (n_cores in cores) {   for (crossval in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {     run <- paste0("radmix_t", n_cores, if (crossval) "_cv" else "_nocv")     run_dir <- file.path(runs_dir, run)     unlink(run_dir, recursive = TRUE)     dir.create(run_dir, recursive = TRUE)     message("Running ", run)     bigparallelr::set_blas_ncores(n_cores)     start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]     hgdp <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(       bed_file,       backingfile = file.path(run_dir, "hgdp_bench"),       quiet = TRUE     )     fit <- gt_radmix(       hgdp,       k = k,       seed = seed,       crossval = crossval,       n_folds = n_folds,       n_cores = n_cores     )     saveRDS(fit, file.path(run_dir, "radmix.rds"))     seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - start     write_q(fit$Q[[1]], file.path(out_dir, "Q", paste0(run, ".Q")))     writeLines(fit$log[[1]], file.path(out_dir, "logs", paste0(run, ".log")))     converged_line <- grep("^Converged in", fit$log[[1]], value = TRUE)[1]     timings[[run]] <- data.frame(       tool = "radmix",       init = "random",       seed = seed,       n_cores = n_cores,       crossval = crossval,       seconds = seconds,       loglik = fit$loglik,       cv_error = if (crossval) fit$cv else NA,       iterations = as.integer(         sub("^Converged in ([0-9]+) iterations.*", "\\1", converged_line)       )     )   } } timings <- do.call(rbind, timings)

code: large_dir <- Sys.getenv("LARGE_DIR", "data/large") dir.create(large_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) n_cores <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("LARGE_CORES", "8")) n_indiv <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("LARGE_N_INDIV", "250000")) n_loci <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("LARGE_N_LOCI", "200000")) k <- 5 # Five ancestral populations, with allele frequencies drawn under the # Balding-Nichols model (Fst = 0.1 from frequencies uniform between 0.05 and # 0.95 in their common ancestor), and five sampled populations of the same # size, whose ancestry proportions are drawn from a Dirichlet # distribution centred on one ancestral population (80% on average, the # rest shared among the other four). The genotypes are binomial draws from # the individual allele frequencies, with 1% of them missing. set.seed(1) pop <- rep(seq_len(k), each = n_indiv / k) alpha <- matrix(0.25, n_indiv, k) alpha[cbind(seq_len(n_indiv), pop)] <- 4 q_true <- matrix(stats::rgamma(n_indiv * k, alpha), n_indiv, k) q_true <- q_true / rowSums(q_true) saveRDS(q_true, file.path(large_dir, "q_true.rds")) # the genotypes, written straight into the backing file of an FBM in blocks # of loci (one byte per genotype, 3 for a missing genotype), on several # cores; each block of loci has its own seed, so the data do not depend on # the number of cores. Each core runs BLAS (for its matrix products) on a # single thread, set in a.FUN, so bigstatsr's check against two levels of # parallelism is not needed options(bigstatsr.check.parallel.blas = FALSE) genotypes <- bigstatsr::FBM.code256(   n_indiv, n_loci,   code = bigsnpr::CODE_012,   backingfile = file.path(large_dir, "sim_fbm"),   init = NULL ) block_size <- 250 invisible(bigstatsr::big_apply(   genotypes,   a.FUN = function(x, ind, q_true, k, block_size) {     bigparallelr::set_blas_ncores(1)     for (j0 in seq(1, length(ind), by = block_size)) {       cols <- ind[j0:min(length(ind), j0 + block_size - 1)]       set.seed(1e6 + cols[1])       f <- 0.1       p_anc <- stats::runif(length(cols), 0.05, 0.95)       p <- matrix(         stats::rbeta(           k * length(cols),           rep(p_anc * (1 - f) / f, each = k),           rep((1 - p_anc) * (1 - f) / f, each = k)         ),         k, length(cols)       )       g <- stats::rbinom(nrow(x) * length(cols), 2, q_true %*% p)       g[stats::runif(length(g)) < 0.01] <- 3L       x[, cols] <- matrix(g, nrow(x))     }     NULL   },   a.combine = "c",   block.size = block_size * 8,   ncores = n_cores,   q_true = q_true,   k = k,   block_size = block_size )) invisible(genotypes$save()) # a PLINK bed file of the genotypes, with the sampled population of each # individual as its family ID, and the loci on 20 chromosomes sim <- structure(   list(     genotypes = genotypes,     fam = data.frame(       family.ID = paste0("pop", pop),       sample.ID = sprintf("ind%06d", seq_len(n_indiv)),       paternal.ID = 0L,       maternal.ID = 0L,       sex = 0L,       affection = -9L     ),     map = data.frame(       chromosome = rep(1:20, each = n_loci / 20),       marker.ID = sprintf("snp%06d", seq_len(n_loci)),       genetic.dist = 0,       physical.pos = rep(seq_len(n_loci / 20) * 1000L, 20),       allele1 = "A",       allele2 = "G"     )   ),   class = "bigSNP" ) bed_file <- bigsnpr::snp_writeBed(sim, file.path(large_dir, "sim_large.bed")) # the FBM is no longer needed: the gen_tibble gets its own backing file rm(sim, genotypes) invisible(gc()) unlink(file.path(large_dir, c("sim_fbm.bk", "sim_fbm.rds"))) # the gen_tibble that gt_radmix() reads, saved so that each run can load it # without reading the bed file again sim_gt <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(   bed_file,   backingfile = file.path(large_dir, "sim_large"),   quiet = TRUE ) invisible(tidypopgen::gt_save(sim_gt, quiet = TRUE)) args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE) run <- args[1] k <- as.integer(args[2]) seed <- as.integer(args[3]) n_cores <- as.integer(args[4]) results_file <- args[5] memory_cap <- args[6] read_mbps <- as.numeric(args[7]) large_dir <- Sys.getenv("LARGE_DIR", "data/large") library(tidygenclust) sim_gt <- tidypopgen::gt_load(file.path(large_dir, "sim_large.gt")) # the bytes read from disk by this process so far (Linux) read_bytes <- function() {   io <- readLines("/proc/self/io")   as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", grep("^read_bytes", io, value = TRUE))) } # whether gt_radmix() will stream the data: it does when the backing file is # larger than 0.8 times the memory available to it (the smaller of the free # memory and the room under its memory cap), and then reads it in chunks stream <- tidygenclust:::radmix_stream_mode(gt_radmix_data(sim_gt)) mem_available <- tidygenclust:::radmix_mem_available() # the peak of the resident memory of this process (Linux): its own memory # plus the pages of the backing file mapped in it peak_rss <- function() {   x <- grep("^VmHWM:", readLines("/proc/self/status"), value = TRUE)   as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", x)) * 1024 } # a memory file of the cgroup of this process (cgroups v2): memory.max is # its cap, and memory.peak the peak of its memory, page cache included # (NA without a cap: the cgroup is then the user's session) cgroup_bytes <- function(name) {   cg <- sub("^0::", "", grep("^0::", readLines("/proc/self/cgroup"),     value = TRUE   ))   f <- file.path("/sys/fs/cgroup", cg, name)   cap <- file.path("/sys/fs/cgroup", cg, "memory.max")   if (!file.exists(f) || readLines(cap) == "max") {     return(NA_real_)   }   as.numeric(readLines(f)) } read_before <- read_bytes() start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] fit <- gt_radmix(sim_gt, k = k, seed = seed, n_cores = n_cores) seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - start read_after <- read_bytes() # the ancestry proportions estimated against those simulated: the clusters # are numbered arbitrarily, so the columns are matched (by the permutation # with the smallest sum of squared differences), then the root mean square # difference is computed q_true <- readRDS(file.path(large_dir, "q_true.rds")) q <- fit$Q[[1]] perms <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(seq_len(k)), k))) perms <- perms[apply(perms, 1, function(x) length(unique(x)) == k), ] sse <- apply(perms, 1, function(x) sum((q[, x] - q_true)^2)) rmse <- sqrt(min(sse) / length(q)) converged_line <- grep("^Converged in", fit$log[[1]], value = TRUE)[1] result <- data.frame(   run = run,   memory_cap = memory_cap,   read_mbps = read_mbps,   n_indiv = nrow(sim_gt),   n_loci = tidypopgen::count_loci(sim_gt),   k = k,   n_cores = n_cores,   seconds = seconds,   iterations = as.integer(     sub("^Converged in ([0-9]+) iterations.*", "\\1", converged_line)   ),   loglik = fit$loglik,   read_gb = (read_after - read_before) / 1e9,   peak_rss_gb = peak_rss() / 1e9,   cgroup_max_gb = cgroup_bytes("memory.max") / 1e9,   cgroup_peak_gb = cgroup_bytes("memory.peak") / 1e9,   data_gb = stream$data_bytes / 1e9,   mem_available_gb = mem_available / 1e9,   streamed = stream$stream,   chunk_mb = stream$chunk_bytes / 2^20,   rmse_q = rmse ) write.table(   result, results_file,   sep = ",", row.names = FALSE,   col.names = !file.exists(results_file),   append = file.exists(results_file) ) print(result) set -euo pipefail large_dir=${LARGE_DIR:-data/large} name=${LARGE_NAME:-large} memory_caps=${LARGE_MEMORY_CAPS:-8G} read_mbps=${LARGE_READ_MBPS:-0 500} out_dir=data/admixture_benchmark mkdir -p "$out_dir" k=5 seed=1 cores=8 bk=$(readlink -f "$large_dir/sim_large.bk") fit=(Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_large_fit.R) runs=$out_dir/${name}_runs.csv peaks=$out_dir/${name}_memory.csv rm -f "$runs" echo "run,peak_anon_gb" > "$peaks"  # the processes started by a process, those they started, and so on descendants() {   local c   for c in $(pgrep -P "$1"); do     echo "$c"     descendants "$c"   done } # run a command, and record the peak of the memory of its processes that is # not the page cache (RssAnon, sampled every 0.2 s), in GB with_peak() {   local run=$1   shift   "$@" &   local pid=$! peak=0 kb p   while kill -0 "$pid" 2> /dev/null; do     for p in $pid $(descendants "$pid"); do       kb=$(awk '/^RssAnon:/ {print $2}' "/proc/$p/status" 2> /dev/null || true)       if [ -n "$kb" ] && [ "$kb" -gt "$peak" ]; then peak=$kb; fi     done     sleep 0.2   done   wait "$pid"   echo "$run,$(awk -v kb="$peak" 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", kb * 1024 / 1e9 }')" \     >> "$peaks" } # drop the pages of the backing file from the page cache (no root needed) drop_cache() {   sync "$bk"   dd if="$bk" iflag=nocache count=0 status=none }  # in memory: the backing file is first read into the page cache cat "$bk" > /dev/null with_peak memory "${fit[@]}" memory $k $seed $cores "$runs" none 0  # with the memory capped, for R and the page cache together, from a cold # page cache: on the disk as it is, in a scope of the user's systemd; with # the reads throttled, in a scope of the system's systemd (as root), in # which R runs as the user, with the environment it needs for mbps in $read_mbps; do   for cap in $memory_caps; do     run=capped_${cap}_$([ "$mbps" = 0 ] && echo ssd || echo "${mbps}mbps")     drop_cache     if [ "$mbps" = 0 ]; then       with_peak "$run" \         systemd-run --user --scope --quiet \         -p MemoryMax="$cap" -p MemorySwapMax=0 \         "${fit[@]}" "$run" $k $seed $cores "$runs" "$cap" 0     else       with_peak "$run" \         sudo systemd-run --scope --quiet \         -p MemoryMax="$cap" -p MemorySwapMax=0 \         -p "IOReadBandwidthMax=$bk ${mbps}M" \         sudo -u "$USER" env "PATH=$PATH" "R_LIBS=${R_LIBS:-}" \         "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" "LARGE_DIR=$large_dir" \         "OMP_PROC_BIND=${OMP_PROC_BIND:-false}" \         "OMP_PLACES=${OMP_PLACES:-threads}" \         "${fit[@]}" "$run" $k $seed $cores "$runs" "$cap" "$mbps"     fi   done done cd vignettes/articles LARGE_DIR=data/mid LARGE_N_INDIV=50000 LARGE_N_LOCI=100000 \   Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_large_data.R sudo -v LARGE_DIR=data/mid LARGE_NAME=mid LARGE_MEMORY_CAPS="4G 1G" \   LARGE_READ_MBPS="0 500 150" taskset -c 0-7 \   bash code/admixture_benchmark_large.sh cd vignettes/articles Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_large_data.R sudo -v taskset -c 0-7 bash code/admixture_benchmark_large.sh

code: library(tidygenclust) start_time <- Sys.time() out_dir <- "data/clumppling_benchmark" dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) # each implementation is timed n_repeats times on each dataset and in each # setting, after a first run (not timed) that loads its code and gives the # results compared n_repeats <- 5 seed <- 1L # py_clumppling() runs the python implementation on a gt_admix object, with # the same arguments as gt_clumppling(); the wrapper is sourced from the # root of the package, where it finds its python module withr::with_dir(   "../..",   source("data-raw/clumppling/py_clumppling.R") ) # the same python module, returning python objects instead of converting # them to R objects, to time the python code alone py_module <- reticulate::import_from_path(   "py_rclumppling",   path = "../../data-raw/clumppling",   convert = FALSE ) # the executables of python (in the conda environment) and R, for the runs # from the command line python <- reticulate::py_exe() rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript") # the example datasets of clumppling, included in tidygenclust: 200 runs of # ADMIXTURE (50 for each K from 2 to 5) on the Cape Verde data of Verdu et # al. (2017), with 399 individuals (capeverde), and 60 runs of STRUCTURE (20 # for each of K = 17, 19 and 21) on the chicken data of Rosenberg et al. # (2001), with 600 chickens capeverde <- readRDS(   system.file("extdata", "capeverde_admix.rds", package = "tidygenclust") ) chicken <- readRDS(   system.file("extdata", "chicken_admix.rds", package = "tidygenclust") ) # the first n runs of each K of a gt_admix object first_runs <- function(x, n) {   keep <- sort(unlist(lapply(split(seq_along(x$k), x$k), utils::head, n)))   x$k <- x$k[keep]   x$Q <- x$Q[keep]   x } # capeverde with 5, 10, 20 and 50 runs for each K, and chicken datasets <- list(   capeverde_5 = first_runs(capeverde, 5),   capeverde_10 = first_runs(capeverde, 10),   capeverde_20 = first_runs(capeverde, 20),   capeverde_50 = capeverde,   chicken_20 = chicken ) # each dataset as a directory of Q files (one for each run, with one row for # each individual and one column for each cluster, as written by ADMIXTURE), # and as a python list of numpy arrays write_q_files <- function(x, q_dir) {   dir.create(q_dir)   for (i in seq_along(x$Q)) {     utils::write.table(       as.matrix(x$Q[[i]]),       file.path(q_dir, sprintf("run%03d.Q", i)),       row.names = FALSE,       col.names = FALSE     )   }   q_dir } to_numpy <- function(x) {   reticulate::r_to_py(lapply(x$Q, function(q) {     reticulate::np_array(       matrix(as.numeric(q), nrow = nrow(q)),       dtype = "float64",       order = "C"     )   })) } inputs <- lapply(names(datasets), function(name) {   list(     admix = datasets[[name]],     q_dir = write_q_files(datasets[[name]], file.path(tempdir(), name)),     q_py = to_numpy(datasets[[name]])   ) }) names(inputs) <- names(datasets) # compare the results of the two implementations: their modes (the runs of # each mode, overall and for each K), their representatives, and, if the # modes are the same, the largest differences between their aligned modes # and their costs across K compare_results <- function(r, py) {   # the modes (named e.g. K2M1) of the values of K that match the pattern   modes_of <- function(res, pattern) {     modes <- res$mode_replicates[grep(pattern, names(res$mode_replicates))]     lapply(modes, as.integer)   }   same_modes <- identical(modes_of(r, ""), modes_of(py, ""))   same_modes_k <- Filter(function(k) {     pattern <- paste0("^K", k, "M")     identical(modes_of(r, pattern), modes_of(py, pattern))   }, r$K_range)   # (the elements of both lists are matched by name)   max_diff <- function(a, b) {     b <- b[names(a)]     max(abs(unlist(lapply(a, as.matrix)) - unlist(lapply(b, as.matrix))))   }   data.frame(     n_modes_r = length(r$mode_replicates),     n_modes_python = length(py$mode_replicates),     same_modes = same_modes,     same_modes_k = paste(same_modes_k, collapse = ", "),     same_representatives = identical(       r$mode_stats$Representative,       py$mode_stats$Representative     ),     max_diff_aligned = if (same_modes) {       max_diff(r$aligned_modes, py$aligned_modes)     } else {       NA     },     max_diff_cost = if (same_modes) {       max_diff(r$cost_acrossK, py$cost_acrossK)     } else {       NA     }   ) } # run a command, stopping if it fails run_command <- function(command, args) {   status <- system2(command, args, stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)   if (status != 0) {     stop("Failed: ", command, " ", paste(args, collapse = " "))   } } # the timed runs of each implementation, in each setting, on an input (a # dataset as a gt_admix object, a directory of Q files and numpy arrays) run_r <- list(   # the Q matrices are in a gt_admix object   memory = function(input) {     gt_clumppling(input$admix, seed = seed)   },   # the Q files are read with tidypopgen::read_q_files()   files = function(input) {     gt_clumppling(tidypopgen::read_q_files(input$q_dir), seed = seed)   },   # a new R process loads tidygenclust, reads the Q files, and saves the   # results in an rds file   command_line = function(input) {     out <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")     on.exit(unlink(out))     run_command(rscript, c("-e", shQuote(sprintf(       paste(         "library(tidygenclust);",         "res <- gt_clumppling(tidypopgen::read_q_files('%s'), seed = %d);",         "saveRDS(res, '%s')"       ),       input$q_dir, seed, out     ))))   } ) run_python <- list(   # the Q matrices are numpy arrays (converted from R before the timing),   # and the results are python objects (not converted to R)   memory = function(input) {     py_module$clumppling_run(Q_list = input$q_py, random_seed = seed)   },   # the Q files are read by clumppling's own parser, which writes the   # processed matrices to a directory and reads them back   files = function(input) {     processed_dir <- tempfile()     on.exit(unlink(processed_dir, recursive = TRUE))     py_module$clumppling_run(       input_dir = input$q_dir,       processed_dir = processed_dir,       random_seed = seed     )   },   # the command-line tool of clumppling, without figures, which reads the Q   # files and writes its results to a directory   command_line = function(input) {     out <- tempfile()     on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))     run_command(python, c(       "-m", "clumppling", "-i", shQuote(input$q_dir), "-o", shQuote(out),       "-f", "admixture", "-v", "False", "--random_seed", seed     ))   } ) timings <- list() agreement <- list() for (name in names(inputs)) {   input <- inputs[[name]]   x <- input$admix   message("Running ", name)   # a first run of each implementation in memory, compared, and a first run   # from the Q files, neither timed   res_r <- suppressMessages(gt_clumppling(x, seed = seed))   res_py <- py_clumppling(x, seed = seed)   agreement[[name]] <- data.frame(     dataset = name,     n_runs = length(x$Q),     n_individuals = nrow(x$Q[[1]]),     k_values = paste(sort(unique(x$k)), collapse = ", "),     compare_results(res_r, res_py)   )   invisible(suppressMessages(run_r$files(input)))   invisible(run_python$files(input))   # then n_repeats timed runs of each, in each setting   for (setting in names(run_r)) {     for (i in seq_len(n_repeats)) {       seconds_r <- system.time(         suppressMessages(run_r[[setting]](input))       )[["elapsed"]]       seconds_py <- system.time(run_python[[setting]](input))[["elapsed"]]       timings[[paste(name, setting, i)]] <- data.frame(         dataset = name,         setting = setting,         repeat_run = i,         implementation = c("r", "python"),         seconds = c(seconds_r, seconds_py)       )     }   } } timings <- do.call(rbind, timings) agreement <- do.call(rbind, agreement) # the time taken to start R and load tidygenclust, and to start python and # load the code of the command-line tool of clumppling startup <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_repeats), function(i) {   data.frame(     repeat_run = i,     implementation = c("r", "python"),     seconds = c(       system.time(         run_command(rscript, c("-e", shQuote("library(tidygenclust)")))       )[["elapsed"]],       system.time(         run_command(python, c("-c", shQuote("import clumppling.__main__")))       )[["elapsed"]]     )   ) }))

code: # all permutations of 1:n permutations <- function(n) {   if (n == 1) {     return(matrix(1))   }   sub <- permutations(n - 1)   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {     cbind(i, matrix(setdiff(seq_len(n), i)[sub], nrow = nrow(sub)))   })) } # reorder the clusters of a gt_admix object with a single run, to best # match those of the Q matrix q_ref match_clusters <- function(adm, q_ref) {   q <- unclass(adm$Q[[1]])   perms <- permutations(ncol(q))   diffs <- apply(perms, 1, function(x) sum(abs(q[, x] - q_ref)))   best <- perms[which.min(diffs), ]   adm$Q[[1]] <- q_matrix(q[, best])   if (!is.null(adm$P)) {     adm$P[[1]] <- adm$P[[1]][, best]   }   adm } q_adm <- unclass(anole_adm$Q[[1]]) anole_radmix <- match_clusters(anole_radmix, q_adm) anole_fm <- match_clusters(anole_fm, q_adm) anole_ada <- match_clusters(anole_ada, q_adm) library(ggplot2) plots <- list(   autoplot(anole_radmix, type = "barplot", k = 3, run = 1,     annotate_group = TRUE   ) +     ggtitle("gt_radmix"),   autoplot(anole_fm, type = "barplot", k = 3, run = 1,     annotate_group = TRUE   ) +     ggtitle("fastmixture"),   autoplot(anole_ada, type = "barplot", k = 3, run = 1,     annotate_group = TRUE   ) +     ggtitle("ADAMIXTURE"),   autoplot(anole_adm, type = "barplot", k = 3, run = 1,     annotate_group = TRUE   ) +     ggtitle("ADMIXTURE") ) patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 1) q_differences <- function(adm) {   q <- unclass(adm$Q[[1]])   c(     max_abs_difference = max(abs(q - q_adm)),     correlation = stats::cor(as.vector(q), as.vector(q_adm))   ) } rbind(   gt_radmix = q_differences(anole_radmix),   fastmixture = q_differences(anole_fm),   ADAMIXTURE = q_differences(anole_ada) ) #>             max_abs_difference correlation #> gt_radmix          0.005020889   0.9999980 #> fastmixture        0.005003755   0.9999981 #> ADAMIXTURE         0.005080578   0.9999979

title: Why pseudohaploids must be declared
text: First, load packages required simulations subsequent analyses. simulations follow ADMIXTURE model, unadmixed individuals populations: n_loci independent loci, frequency alternate allele drawn uniform distribution 0.05 0.95 common ancestral population. population drifts ancestral population: alternative allele frequency locus drawn independently population Balding-Nichols model (Balding & Nichols 1995), beta distribution ancestral frequency p mean variance fst * p * (1 - p). larger fst , populations differ. diploid individual carries two independently sampled alleles locus, probability sampling alternate allele given population-specific frequency. resulting genotype therefore follows binomial distribution two trials, takes values 0, 1 2. pseudohaploid individual carries single sampled allele locus, drawn according population-specific allele frequency. mimics random selection single allele site: heterozygous site, either allele equally likely selected. Consequently, across individuals, probability observing alternate allele equal population frequency. genotype stored 0 2. simulated data contain missing genotypes, linkage loci admixture, true number clusters equals number populations. function simulate_pseudohaploids() implements steps. populations numbers diploid pseudohaploid individuals given named vectors. returns gen_tibble pseudohaploids coded 0/2 declared, read file (true allele frequencies populations attribute “frequencies”): function defined vignettes/articles/code/pseudohaploid_simulation.R (source code package), can loaded source() simulate designs. first example, simulate two populations, B, diverged common ancestor F_ST 0.1. dataset comprises 5,000 loci, 20 diploid individuals populations B, additional 40 pseudohaploid individuals population . pseudohaploids heterozygous genotypes: function gt_pseudohaploid() identifies :
code: library(tidygenclust) library(tidypopgen) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) # Simulate diploid and pseudohaploid individuals from a few populations. # n_diploid and n_pseudohaploid are named vectors with the number of # individuals of each population (a population missing from one of them has # none of that type), e.g. n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20) and # n_pseudohaploid = c(A = 40). The allele frequencies of each population # drift from those of a common ancestral population (with the given F_ST). # Returns a gen_tibble with the columns id, population and type ("diploid" or # "pseudohaploid"), in which the pseudohaploids are coded 0/2 but not # declared as pseudohaploids, as when they are read from a file. The true # allele frequencies of the populations (a matrix with one row per locus and # one column per population) are in its attribute "frequencies" simulate_pseudohaploids <- function(n_diploid, n_pseudohaploid = c(),                                     n_loci = 5000, fst = 0.1, seed = NULL) {   if (!is.null(seed)) {     set.seed(seed)   }   populations <- union(names(n_diploid), names(n_pseudohaploid))   # the number of individuals of a population in n (0 if it is not in n)   count <- function(n, pop) if (pop %in% names(n)) n[[pop]] else 0   # the frequency of the alternate allele of each locus in the ancestral   # population   p_ancestral <- stats::runif(n_loci, 0.05, 0.95)   frequencies <- list()   genotypes <- list()   indiv_meta <- list()   for (pop in populations) {     # the frequencies in this population, drifted from the ancestral ones     # (Balding-Nichols model: a beta distribution with mean p_ancestral and     # variance fst * p_ancestral * (1 - p_ancestral))     p_pop <- frequencies[[pop]] <- stats::rbeta(       n_loci,       p_ancestral * (1 - fst) / fst,       (1 - p_ancestral) * (1 - fst) / fst     )     # n individuals with `copies` copies of each locus, each copy carrying     # the alternate allele with probability p_pop (one row per individual)     draw <- function(n, copies) {       matrix(         stats::rbinom(n * n_loci, copies, p_pop),         ncol = n_loci, byrow = TRUE       )     }     # a diploid carries two copies; a pseudohaploid carries one, stored as a     # homozygous genotype (0 or 2), as in tidypopgen     n_dip <- count(n_diploid, pop)     n_pseudo <- count(n_pseudohaploid, pop)     genotypes[[pop]] <- rbind(draw(n_dip, 2), 2 * draw(n_pseudo, 1))     indiv_meta[[pop]] <- data.frame(       population = rep(pop, n_dip + n_pseudo),       type = rep(c("diploid", "pseudohaploid"), c(n_dip, n_pseudo))     )   }   indiv_meta <- do.call(rbind, indiv_meta)   indiv_meta <- data.frame(     id = paste0("ind", seq_len(nrow(indiv_meta))),     indiv_meta   )   loci <- data.frame(     name = paste0("rs", seq_len(n_loci)),     chromosome = 1L,     position = seq_len(n_loci),     genetic_dist = 0,     allele_ref = "A",     allele_alt = "T"   )   gt <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(     do.call(rbind, genotypes),     indiv_meta = indiv_meta,     loci = loci,     backingfile = tempfile("pseudohaploids_"),     quiet = TRUE   )   attr(gt, "frequencies") <- do.call(cbind, frequencies)   gt } gt <- simulate_pseudohaploids(   n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20),   n_pseudohaploid = c(A = 40),   fst = 0.1,   seed = 1 ) gt #> # A gen_tibble: 5000 loci #> # A tibble:     80 × 4 #>    id    population type     genotypes #>    <chr> <chr>      <chr>   <vctr_SNP> #>  1 ind1  A          diploid  [0,1,...] #>  2 ind2  A          diploid  [0,0,...] #>  3 ind3  A          diploid  [0,0,...] #>  4 ind4  A          diploid  [1,0,...] #>  5 ind5  A          diploid  [0,2,...] #>  6 ind6  A          diploid  [0,0,...] #>  7 ind7  A          diploid  [0,1,...] #>  8 ind8  A          diploid  [0,1,...] #>  9 ind9  A          diploid  [0,1,...] #> 10 ind10 A          diploid  [0,1,...] #> # ℹ 70 more rows table(gt$population, gt$type) #>     #>     diploid pseudohaploid #>   A      20            40 #>   B      20             0 heterozygosity <- rowMeans(show_genotypes(gt) == 1) tapply(heterozygosity, gt$type, mean) #>       diploid pseudohaploid  #>      0.323615      0.000000 gt_declared <- gt_pseudohaploid(gt) table(type = gt$type, ploidy = indiv_ploidy(gt_declared)) #>                ploidy #> type             1  2 #>   diploid        0 40 #>   pseudohaploid 40  0

code: library(tidygenclust) library(tidypopgen) source("code/pseudohaploid_simulation.R") start_time <- Sys.time() out_dir <- "data/pseudohaploids" dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) # each replicate simulates a dataset with its own seed (also used for the # fits), so every dataset can be simulated again on its own replicates <- 1:5 n_cores <- min(4L, parallel::detectCores()) # Analyse a dataset for each value of k, with cross-validation, twice: with # the pseudohaploids undeclared (treated as diploids) and declared with # gt_pseudohaploid(). Returns the log-likelihood and cross-validation error # of each fit (fits), and, if with_q is TRUE, the ancestry proportions of # each individual for each k > 1 (q, in long format) analyse <- function(gt, k, seed, with_q = FALSE) {   fits <- list()   q <- list()   for (treatment in c("undeclared", "declared")) {     x <- if (treatment == "declared") gt_pseudohaploid(gt) else gt     adm <- gt_radmix(       x,       k = k,       seed = seed,       crossval = TRUE,       n_cores = n_cores     )     fits[[treatment]] <- data.frame(       treatment = treatment,       k = adm$k,       loglik = adm$loglik,       cv = adm$cv     )     if (with_q) {       for (i in which(adm$k > 1)) {         q_i <- unclass(adm$Q[[i]])         q[[paste(treatment, i)]] <- data.frame(           treatment = treatment,           k = adm$k[i],           id = gt$id,           population = gt$population,           type = gt$type,           cluster = rep(seq_len(ncol(q_i)), each = nrow(q_i)),           q = round(as.vector(q_i), 4)         )       }     }   }   list(fits = do.call(rbind, fits), q = do.call(rbind, q)) } # three scenarios, all with 5,000 loci and two populations (so the true K is # 2): pseudohaploids in one of the two populations, with moderate (F_ST = # 0.1) or weak (F_ST = 0.05) structure; and a population known only from # pseudohaploids (e.g. ancient samples), next to a diploid population scenarios <- list(   pseudohaploids_in_a = list(     n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20), n_pseudohaploid = c(A = 40), fst = 0.1   ),   weak_structure = list(     n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20), n_pseudohaploid = c(A = 40), fst = 0.05   ),   b_pseudohaploid = list(     n_diploid = c(A = 20), n_pseudohaploid = c(B = 40), fst = 0.1   ) ) # each scenario is analysed for K = 1 to 6 fits <- list() q <- list() for (scenario in names(scenarios)) {   for (replicate in replicates) {     message("Scenario ", scenario, ", replicate ", replicate)     s <- scenarios[[scenario]]     gt <- simulate_pseudohaploids(       n_diploid = s$n_diploid,       n_pseudohaploid = s$n_pseudohaploid,       fst = s$fst,       seed = replicate     )     res <- analyse(gt, k = 1:6, seed = replicate, with_q = TRUE)     run <- paste(scenario, replicate)     fits[[run]] <- data.frame(scenario, replicate, res$fits)     q[[run]] <- data.frame(scenario, replicate, res$q)   } } fits <- do.call(rbind, fits) q <- do.call(rbind, q) # when does cross-validation prefer K = 2 over K = 1? 20 diploids from each # population, and 0 to 80 pseudohaploids from population A, with weak to # moderate structure (K = 1 and 2 only) grid <- expand.grid(   fst = c(0.03, 0.05, 0.1),   n_pseudohaploid = c(0, 20, 40, 80),   replicate = replicates ) grid_fits <- list() for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid))) {   message("Grid ", i, " of ", nrow(grid))   gt <- simulate_pseudohaploids(     n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20),     n_pseudohaploid = c(A = grid$n_pseudohaploid[i]),     fst = grid$fst[i],     seed = grid$replicate[i]   )   res <- analyse(gt, k = 1:2, seed = grid$replicate[i])   grid_fits[[i]] <- data.frame(grid[i, ], res$fits, row.names = NULL) } grid_fits <- do.call(rbind, grid_fits) # why do the individuals of the larger population appear slightly admixed # at K = 2? Two populations of different or equal sizes, with or without # pseudohaploids, fitted at K = 2 with the allele frequencies estimated (with # the pseudohaploids undeclared and declared), and with the allele # frequencies fixed at their true values (pseudohaploids declared) sample_size_designs <- list(   equal = list(n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20), n_pseudohaploid = c()),   a_larger = list(n_diploid = c(A = 60, B = 20), n_pseudohaploid = c()),   pseudohaploids_in_a = list(     n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 20), n_pseudohaploid = c(A = 40)   ),   b_larger = list(n_diploid = c(A = 20, B = 60), n_pseudohaploid = c(A = 40)) ) # more replicates than above, as the differences are small sample_size_replicates <- 1:10 sample_size <- list() for (design in names(sample_size_designs)) {   for (replicate in sample_size_replicates) {     message("Design ", design, ", replicate ", replicate)     d <- sample_size_designs[[design]]     gt <- simulate_pseudohaploids(       n_diploid = d$n_diploid,       n_pseudohaploid = d$n_pseudohaploid,       fst = 0.1,       seed = replicate     )     fit <- function(x, frequencies) {       adm <- gt_radmix(         x,         k = 2,         seed = replicate,         n_cores = n_cores,         init_p = if (frequencies == "true") attr(gt, "frequencies"),         fix_p = frequencies == "true"       )       q_i <- unclass(adm$Q[[1]])       # the cluster of each population: with the true frequencies, the       # column of the population; otherwise, the cluster with the largest       # mean ancestry among its individuals       own <- if (frequencies == "true") {         c(A = 1, B = 2)       } else {         sapply(c(A = "A", B = "B"), function(pop) {           unname(which.max(colMeans(q_i[gt$population == pop, ])))         })       }       own <- own[gt$population]       # the mean ancestry of each group from the other cluster       other <- 1 - q_i[cbind(seq_len(nrow(q_i)), own)]       data.frame(         design = design,         replicate = replicate,         frequencies = frequencies,         stats::aggregate(           list(other = other),           list(population = gt$population, type = gt$type),           mean         )       )     }     runs <- list(       fit(gt_pseudohaploid(gt), "estimated"),       fit(gt_pseudohaploid(gt), "true")     )     runs[[1]]$treatment <- runs[[2]]$treatment <- "declared"     if (length(d$n_pseudohaploid) > 0) {       runs[[3]] <- fit(gt, "estimated")       runs[[3]]$treatment <- "undeclared"     }     sample_size[[paste(design, replicate)]] <- do.call(rbind, runs)   } } sample_size <- do.call(rbind, sample_size) cd vignettes/articles Rscript code/pseudohaploid_runs.R

code: clump_res %>% tidy(matrix = "modes") ## # A tibble: 7 × 3 ##       k     m label ##   <dbl> <dbl> <chr> ## 1     2     1 K2M1  ## 2     3     1 K3M1  ## 3     4     1 K4M1  ## 4     4     2 K4M2  ## 5     5     1 K5M1  ## 6     5     2 K5M2  ## 7     5     3 K5M3 clump_res %>% tidy(matrix = "major_modes") ## # A tibble: 4 × 3 ##       k     m label ##   <dbl> <dbl> <chr> ## 1     2     1 K2M1  ## 2     3     1 K3M1  ## 3     4     1 K4M1  ## 4     5     1 K5M1 q_modes <- clump_res %>% tidy(matrix = "Q_modes") q_modes %>% names() ## [1] "K2M1" "K3M1" "K4M1" "K4M2" "K5M1" "K5M2" "K5M3" q_major_modes <- clump_res %>% tidy(matrix = "Q_major_modes") q_major_modes %>% names() ## [1] "K2M1" "K3M1" "K4M1" "K5M1" q4_tidied <- q_major_modes[["K4M1"]] q4_tidied %>% head() ## # A tibble: 6 × 3 ##      id q     percentage ##   <int> <chr>      <dbl> ## 1     1 1      0.0000100 ## 2     1 2      0.0000100 ## 3     1 3      0.0000100 ## 4     1 4      1.000     ## 5     2 1      0.0000100 ## 6     2 2      0.0000100 library(ggplot2) # set up the ggplot object plt <- q4_tidied %>% ggplot(   aes(     x = id,     y = percentage,     fill = q   ) ) +   # add the columns based on percentage membership to each cluster   geom_col(     width = 1,     position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)   ) +   # set the y label   labs(y = "K = 4") +   # use a theme to match the distruct look, removing most decorations   theme_distruct() +   # set the colour scale to be the same as in distruct and clumppling   scale_fill_distruct()  plt plt + scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") ## Scale for fill is already present. ## Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
